area: RespawnAnchorBlock behaviour on Minecraft 26.2 (Mojang official mappings) — charge/explode/set-spawn condition tree, explosion parameters, and the client-visible replacement for the now-removed DimensionType.respawnAnchorWorks()

Registered as: register("gameplay/respawn_anchor_works", EnvironmentAttribute.builder(AttributeTypes.BOOLEAN).defaultValue(false)) — NO .syncable(), NO .notPositional(). So isSyncable()==false and isPositional()==true. Identifier: minecraft:gameplay/respawn_anchor_works.

Declared abstract on Level (plus a covariant bridge 'public EnvironmentAttributeReader environmentAttributes()'), so ClientLevel implements it — the call compiles and runs client-side. ClientLevel overrides it as 'public EnvironmentAttributeSystem environmentAttributes()'.

Backed by a private final field built in the constructor: this.environmentAttributes = this.addEnvironmentAttributeLayers(EnvironmentAttributeSystem.builder()).build(); addEnvironmentAttributeLayers calls environmentAttributes.addDefaultLayers(this) and then only adds time-based layers for SKY_COLOR and SKY_LIGHT_FACTOR.

Default method: returns this.getValue(attribute, Vec3.atCenterOf(pos)). EnvironmentAttributeSystem implements EnvironmentAttributeReader, so this overload is callable on the value returned by ClientLevel.environmentAttributes(). This is the overload canSetSpawn uses.

Do NOT call this with RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS: EnvironmentAttributeSystem.getDimensionValue throws new IllegalStateException("Position must always be provided for positional attribute " + attribute) when SharedConstants.IS_RUNNING_IN_IDE && attribute.isPositional(), which is exactly the Loom dev-client case.

Body: sampler = getValueSampler(attribute); return sampler == null ? attribute.defaultValue() : sampler.getValue(pos, biomeInterpolator); — a missing layer silently yields the attribute default rather than throwing. This is the mechanism that makes the client answer 'false' everywhere.

NETWORK_CODEC = CODEC.xmap(EnvironmentAttributeMap::filterSyncable, EnvironmentAttributeMap::filterSyncable), and private static filterSyncable does Maps.filterKeys(entries, EnvironmentAttribute::isSyncable). Applied on DECODE as well as encode.

= createDirectCodec(EnvironmentAttributeMap.NETWORK_CODEC), while DIRECT_CODEC = createDirectCodec(EnvironmentAttributeMap.CODEC). The 'attributes' field is attributeMapCodec.optionalFieldOf("attributes", EnvironmentAttributeMap.EMPTY).
Record component. DimensionType is now 'public final class DimensionType extends java.lang.Record'.

DOES NOT EXIST in 26.2. Confirmed by a full 'javap -p net.minecraft.world.level.dimension.DimensionType' — the record's components are hasFixedTime, hasSkyLight, hasCeiling, hasEnderDragonFight, coordinateScale, minY, height, logicalHeight, infiniburn, ambientLight, monsterSettings, skybox, cardinalLightType, attributes, timelines, defaultClock. The flag moved into attributes() as EnvironmentAttributes.RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS. (bedWorks() is likewise gone; it is now EnvironmentAttributes.BED_RULE.)

A plain record component, always synced (not part of the attributes map). true for minecraft:the_nether AND minecraft:overworld_caves, so it is NOT a correct proxy for respawn_anchor_works (overworld_caves reuses overworldAttributes, which sets RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS=false).

signatures.notes: Still present in 26.2. 'level.dimension() == Level.NETHER' is the simplest exact client-side test for the vanilla dimension set.

register("gameplay/fast_lava", builder(BOOLEAN).defaultValue(false).notPositional().syncable()) — the only nether-exclusive gameplay boolean that is BOTH syncable and notPositional, so getDimensionValue() is legal on it client-side. In DimensionTypes.bootstrap only minecraft:the_nether sets it (true). Best client-side proxy for 'respawn anchor works here'.

Both .syncable(). WATER_EVAPORATES defaultValue(false), nether sets true. PIGLINS_ZOMBIFY defaultValue(true), nether sets false. Equivalent client-readable nether proxies. BED_RULE, by contrast, is NOT syncable, so the client cannot read 'bed explodes' either.
Ground truth for RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS: overworldAttributes sets it false (shared by minecraft:overworld and minecraft:overworld_caves); minecraft:the_nether sets true; minecraft:the_end sets false.

Contains 'new RegistryData(Registries.DIMENSION_TYPE, DimensionType.NETWORK_CODEC)'. WORLDGEN_REGISTRIES (server/datapack side) uses DimensionType.DIRECT_CODEC instead. This is the exact point where the client loses non-syncable attributes.

Uses this.data.elementCodec() for BOTH branches — PendingRegistration.loadFromNetwork(...) when the packet carried contents, and PendingRegistration.findAndLoadFromResource(..., knownDataPathConverter, knownDataSource) when contents were skipped because the client shares the KnownPack. So even the locally-read vanilla dimension_type JSON is decoded through NETWORK_CODEC and stripped.

The client-side call site proving the client builds its dimension_type registry with SYNCHRONIZED_REGISTRIES (hence NETWORK_CODEC). Applies in singleplayer too — RegistrySynchronization.packRegistry encodes with registryData.elementCodec() into an NBT Tag before the client decodes it.

The overload RespawnAnchorBlock.explode uses. Decompiled param names: (source, damageSource, @Nullable damageCalculator, boomPos, r, fire, blockInteraction). It forwards to the 13-arg abstract explode with ParticleTypes.EXPLOSION, ParticleTypes.EXPLOSION_EMITTER, DEFAULT_EXPLOSION_BLOCK_PARTICLES, SoundEvents.GENERIC_EXPLODE. Only ServerLevel implements the abstract one meaningfully.

signatures.notes: The anchor passes BLOCK.
Reached via level.damageSources(); Level.damageSources() is public and non-abstract, so it exists on ClientLevel too.

The anchor passes an anonymous subclass overriding ONLY this method: return testPos.equals(pos) && inWater ? Optional.of(Blocks.WATER.getExplosionResistance()) : super.getBlockExplosionResistance(...). Everything else (shouldBlockExplode, shouldDamageEntity, getKnockbackMultiplier, getEntityDamageAmount) is vanilla default.

signatures.member: SUCCESS / SUCCESS_SERVER / CONSUME (all InteractionResult$Success) ; FAIL (Fail) ; PASS (Pass) ; TRY_WITH_EMPTY_HAND (TryEmptyHandInteraction)
signatures.notes: sealed interface. Success.consumesAction() returns true — so SUCCESS, SUCCESS_SERVER and CONSUME all consume; the default consumesAction() is false, so PASS, FAIL and TRY_WITH_EMPTY_HAND do not. signatures.member: public static final net.minecraft.sounds.SoundEvent RESPAWN_ANCHOR_AMBIENT / RESPAWN_ANCHOR_CHARGE / RESPAWN_ANCHOR_SET_SPAWN ; public static final net.minecraft.core.Holder$Reference<net.minecraft.sounds.SoundEvent> RESPAWN_ANCHOR_DEPLETE
signatures.notes: Note the type asymmetry: DEPLETE is a Holder.Reference<SoundEvent>, the other three are bare SoundEvent. DEPLETE is not used by RespawnAnchorBlock at all.
Second arg is @Nullable LivingEntity; useItemOn passes the player.

gotchas: Q1 — the biggest structural change: useItemOn no longer explodes or sets spawn. In 26.2 RespawnAnchorBlock.useItemOn does exactly one thing, charging, and everything else lives in useWithoutItem. Full tree. (a) CHARGE: useItemOn, when isRespawnFuel(itemStack) && canBeCharged(state) -> charge(player, level, pos, state); itemStack.consume(1, player); returns InteractionResult.SUCCESS. There is no isClientSide gate, so this body also runs on the client inside MultiPlayerGameMode.startPrediction. (b) EXPLODE: useWithoutItem, when state.getValue(CHARGE) != 0 && level instanceof ServerLevel && !canSetSpawn(serverLevel, pos) -> this.explode(state, serverLevel, pos); returns InteractionResult.SUCCESS_SERVER. (c) SET SPAWN: useWithoutItem, when charge != 0 && ServerLevel && canSetSpawn && player instanceof ServerPlayer && (getRespawnConfig() == null || !isSamePosition(newConfig)) -> setRespawnPosition(newConfig, true) + RESPAWN_ANCHOR_SET_SPAWN sound; returns SUCCESS_SERVER. (d) NOTHING: useWithoutItem returns PASS when charge == 0; returns CONSUME on the client (level is not a ServerLevel); returns CONSUME when the spawn point is already this exact position or the player is not a ServerPlayer. useItemOn returns PASS in exactly one case — hand == MAIN_HAND && off-hand holds glowstone && canBeCharged — which deliberately lets the interaction fall through so the off-hand pass does the charging; otherwise it returns TRY_WITH_EMPTY_HAND, which is what makes the caller invoke useWithoutItem.

Q1 corollary — a full (4-charge) anchor with glowstone in hand still explodes/sets spawn. isRespawnFuel is true but canBeCharged is false, so useItemOn falls to the ternary, whose canBeCharged term is also false, so it returns TRY_WITH_EMPTY_HAND and useWithoutItem runs. Also, useWithoutItem is only reached when hand == InteractionHand.MAIN_HAND (guard in both ServerPlayerGameMode and MultiPlayerGameMode), so an off-hand-only interaction can never explode an anchor. And nothing in useWithoutItem decrements CHARGE — setting spawn does not consume a charge.

Q2 — a 1-charge anchor explodes exactly as hard as a 4-charge one. explode() never reads CHARGE (it removes the block first with level.removeBlock(pos, false), so the state param is effectively unused for scaling). Exact call: level.explode(null, level.damageSources().badRespawnPointExplosion(boomPos), damageCalculator, boomPos, 5.0F, true, ExplosionInteraction.BLOCK) with boomPos = Vec3.atCenterOf(pos). So radius/power = 5.0F, fire = true, interaction = BLOCK, source entity = null. The ExplosionDamageCalculator is an anonymous subclass that overrides only getBlockExplosionResistance, returning Optional.of(Blocks.WATER.getExplosionResistance()) (= 100.0F) when testPos.equals(pos) && inWater, and super otherwise — so it damps block-breaking only at the anchor's own position, and does not change entity damage or knockback.

Q6 — isWaterThatWouldFlow does NOT gate charging, and does NOT prevent the explosion. It is called only inside explode(), after the block is already removed, to compute inWater = (any HORIZONTAL neighbour isWaterThatWouldFlow) || level.getFluidState(pos.above()).is(FluidTags.WATER). Its only effect is the 100.0F resistance substitution at the anchor position described above. The charging path (isRespawnFuel + canBeCharged) never touches fluids at all, so water adjacency neither blocks nor allows charging.

Q5 — the headline client-side trap. canSetSpawn's whole body is level.environmentAttributes().getValue(EnvironmentAttributes.RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS, pos), and Level.environmentAttributes() is public abstract with a public ClientLevel override, so calling that exact expression on a ClientLevel COMPILES AND RUNS — and always returns false, in every dimension, including the Nether. RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS is registered without .syncable(); DimensionType is synced to the client with DimensionType.NETWORK_CODEC (RegistryDataLoader.SYNCHRONIZED_REGISTRIES), which uses EnvironmentAttributeMap.NETWORK_CODEC = CODEC.xmap(filterSyncable, filterSyncable); filterSyncable drops every non-syncable key on decode as well as encode. NetworkRegistryLoadTask applies the same elementCodec to the local known-pack JSON path, so the stripping happens in singleplayer too. With no layer registered, EnvironmentAttributeSystem.getValue falls back to attribute.defaultValue(), which is false. This fails silently — no exception, no log line, just a wrong boolean.

Q5 — the other trap on the same call: RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS never calls .notPositional(), and EnvironmentAttribute.Builder defaults isPositional = true. EnvironmentAttributeSystem.getDimensionValue throws IllegalStateException("Position must always be provided for positional attribute ...") whenever SharedConstants.IS_RUNNING_IN_IDE — i.e. it throws in a Loom dev client but not in a shipped jar. Always use the getValue(attribute, BlockPos) overload for this attribute.

Q5 — what a ClientLevel can actually call, in order of correctness. (1) Authoritative, dev/singleplayer only: if (Minecraft.getInstance().hasSingleplayerServer()) { ServerLevel sl = Minecraft.getInstance().getSingleplayerServer().getLevel(clientLevel.dimension()); if (sl != null) return RespawnAnchorBlock.canSetSpawn(sl, pos); } — real server data, but that ServerLevel is owned by the integrated server thread, so treat it as a read-only probe and do not touch it from a render callback. (2) Multiplayer-safe proxy: clientLevel.environmentAttributes().getDimensionValue(EnvironmentAttributes.FAST_LAVA) — FAST_LAVA is .notPositional().syncable() (so both readable and legal via getDimensionValue) and in DimensionTypes.bootstrap only minecraft:the_nether sets it true, which is also the only dimension setting RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS true. WATER_EVAPORATES (syncable, nether-only true) and PIGLINS_ZOMBIFY (syncable, nether sets false) work identically. (3) clientLevel.dimension() == Level.NETHER — exact for the vanilla dimension set, blind to datapack dimensions. (4) Do NOT use dimensionType().hasCeiling(): it is also true for minecraft:overworld_caves, which sets RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS=false. There is no fully general client-visible answer, because a datapack can set respawn_anchor_works on a custom dimension and that value is never transmitted.

Q3 — isRespawnFuel is one line: itemInHand.is(Items.GLOWSTONE). Glowstone the block item only; there is no tag, no ItemTags indirection, and glowstone dust does not work. The method is private static, so a mod has to re-implement the check rather than call it.

Q4 — canBeCharged is one line: state.getValue(CHARGE) < 4, with the literal 4 rather than MAX_CHARGES. Also private static. Reproduce as state.getValue(RespawnAnchorBlock.CHARGE) < RespawnAnchorBlock.MAX_CHARGES.

Q7 — RespawnAnchorBlock.CHARGE is BlockStateProperties.RESPAWN_ANCHOR_CHARGES = IntegerProperty.create("charges", 0, 4): blockstate key "charges", values 0 through 4 inclusive (5 states). BlockStateProperties also exposes MIN_RESPAWN_ANCHOR_CHARGES = 0 and MAX_RESPAWN_ANCHOR_CHARGES = 4, mirrored on the block as MIN_CHARGES/MAX_CHARGES. state.getValue(CHARGE) returns Integer, so a raw == comparison against a boxed value is a bug; compare as int.

Other 26.2 renames that will bite a port: DimensionType is now a record and has lost both respawnAnchorWorks() and bedWorks() — bed behaviour moved to EnvironmentAttributes.BED_RULE (a BedRule enum, values include CAN_SLEEP_WHEN_DARK and EXPLODES), which like RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS is NOT syncable, so the client cannot read 'beds explode here' either. ServerPlayer.setRespawnPosition now takes (ServerPlayer.RespawnConfig, boolean) built from LevelData.RespawnData.of(ResourceKey<Level>, BlockPos, float, float). InteractionResult is a sealed interface, not an enum — SUCCESS_SERVER and TRY_WITH_EMPTY_HAND are new, and TRY_WITH_EMPTY_HAND is the only value that triggers the useWithoutItem fallback, so a mixin that returns FAIL or PASS from useItemOn silently disables the explode path.

Uncallable-as-written summary: RespawnAnchorBlock.explode is private, an instance method, and takes ServerLevel — three separate reasons a client mod cannot reach it. canSetSpawn is public static but its ServerLevel parameter makes it uncallable with a ClientLevel. isRespawnFuel, canBeCharged and isWaterThatWouldFlow are all private static. Only charge(), CHARGE, MIN_CHARGES/MAX_CHARGES, getScaledChargeLevel and findStandUpPosition (CollisionGetter, so ClientLevel-friendly) are genuinely public API.
